question: The EU’s single market operates on the premise that EU law is applied uniformly and consistently in all Member States. This is particularly relevant when it comes to the regulatory qualification of commercial products, since divergent approaches among national authorities lead to distortions of competition and legal uncertainty.

In January 2024, as part of the work of the Standing Committee on Plants, Animals, Food and Feed (SCoPAFF), SILTAC was reclassified in Commission working document ‘Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009 – scope and borderline issues’. It was categorised as a plant protection product (PPP), despite having previously spent years on the EU market as a non-PPP.

This change has been implemented to varying degrees and in different ways by the national authorities of the individual Member States, leading to disparate market effects depending on the country. In light of the above: 1.
Is the Commission monitoring the way in which the Member States are applying SILTAC’s reclassification arising from the SCoPAFF working document?
Is it aware of the national authorities’ divergent approaches to this reclassification and their impact on the functioning of the EU internal market?
What action is it taking or planning to take in order to prevent market fragmentation as a result of the non-uniform application of the qualification of a specific product?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.9.

2026) The Commission refers the Honourable Members to the replies to E-001536/261 and E000469/262, which explain in detail the procedure followed to determine whether SILTAC falls within the scope of Regulation (EC) No 1107/20093, the role of the Standing Committee on Plants, Animals, Food and Feed, Section Phytopharmaceuticals – Legislation (‘SCoPAFF’), and of the related scope document4, as a coordination tool between Member States and the Commission, aimed at supporting a coherent and harmonised application of the existing legal framework in technically complex or borderline situations.
The Commission is not aware of market fragmentation as regards the product SILTAC, as all Member States agree that the product is within the scope of Regulation (EC) No 1107/20095.

It has discussed with Member States possibilities for leniency in enforcement provided that the manufacturer takes the necessary steps to seek approval of the active substance(s) and authorisation of the product under that Regulation, thereby regularising its legal situation.
The manufacturer could approach a Member State willing to become the rapporteur for the initial risk assessment for advice, including the Member State where the manufacturer is based (Poland).

However, at the meeting of SCoPAFF on 29-30 June 20266, the Member States informed that so far none of them had been contacted by the manufacturer of SILTAC with a view to submitting an application for the approval of the active substance(s) and the subsequent authorisation of the product.

The Commission will continue to work with Member States towards a coherent and uniform application and enforcement of the provisions of Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009 to prevent fragmentation of the internal market.
